correctness.rationale: Definitions and all quantifiers are explicit for one finite 18-vertex graph. Parity is a proved invariant under any even cycle. Enumerator A checks 42 matchings, 120 labeled colouring states, 216 six-cycle edges, component decomposition and all-pairs distances; enumerator B independently constructs 120 states by point-by-point assignments and 18 static hexagons, recovers exactly the same ordered state and 216-edge arrays, hub incidence and every component eccentricity. Both programs actually ran successfully and agree on canonical SHA-256 data; the complete data certificate is embedded. Thus finite exhaustive enumeration is an exact proof here, not a finite test extrapolated to arbitrary graph size.

originality.rationale: The closest earlier Pappus result is an exact 20-vertex/36-edge three-edge-colouring Kempe graph MODULO colour-name permutations, two copies of K1 joined with three K3, and a matching-sign parity obstruction; none of those quotient facts is new. The present theorem instead computes the six-sheeted named-colour, six-cycle-ONLY covering and proves it consists of two connected alternating-hexagon thickenings T(K3,3), with 216 moves, diameter six and unrestricted-versus-local metric comparison. An abstract quotient graph, even with its number of colourings and sign classes, cannot determine its six-sheeted covering or the lengths of paths in that cover: trivial and nontrivial coverings of the same quotient can have different components and metrics. Other published works treat four-colour equivalence, general Kempe graphs and aggregate unrestricted three-colour counts. Exact primary-text and record comparisons revealed no dominating statement for the labelled local covering, though indexed or supplementary coverage remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: Hexagon switching is the shortest nontrivial edge-Kempe operation on this canonical girth-six 18-vertex configuration. Exact local reachability, two complete parity classes, 216 transitions, all component distances, and an explicit alternating hexagon-thickened K3,3 model answer a motivated reconfiguration question that cannot be inferred from mere colouring counts or unrestricted class numbers. The separation of restricted diameter six from unrestricted diameter four is a nontrivial measure of locality cost; the structural model explains all vertex degrees. The earlier 10-vertex quotient has diameter two, whereas the newly identified named-colour cover has diameter six; this is a substantive labelled configuration distinction and not a one-parameter increment.
